# Raw HTML and render options {#html}

Raw HTML passthrough was a trusted-content default in 0.1: a host that rendered user input and forgot the flag shipped an XSS hole. In 0.2 `rawHtml` defaults to false, and raw blocks and spans are escaped unless the host opts in ([#2683](https://github.com/markup-carve/carve/issues/2683), C2-H-050, C2-H-051). Review every render option instead of reusing a 0.1 options object.

Tool: Review by hand.

````text
```
````

**U-248** <Badge type="danger" text="report" /> <Badge type="warning" text="silent" /> Under C2-H-176, `c` followed by U+007F and `d` writes the control character itself between `c` and `d` in 0.1 HTML.
Tool: Review the replacement character.

::: compare no-render
```text
c⟨U+007F⟩d
```
```text
<p>c�d</p> C2-H-176 replaces a rejected control character such as U+007F, U+000B, or U+0085 with U+FFFD in HTML text; 0.1 wrote the character itself, `<p>c` U+007F `d</p>`. The example holds U+007F, since the map holds no escaped character and JSON has no unescaped U+000B.
```
:::

**U-262** <Badge type="danger" text="report" /> <Badge type="warning" text="silent" /> Under C2-H-116, an authored attribute with a reserved carrier name, as in `[t]{data-carve-raw=html}`, passed through in 0.1 when `roundtrip` was off.
Tool: Rename the attribute.

::: compare no-render
```text
[t]{data-carve-raw=html}
```
```text
<p><span>t</span></p> C2-H-116: an authored attribute with a reserved carrier name is dropped with `roundtrip` on or off, and `carrier-attribute-dropped` reports it.
```
:::

**U-287** <Badge type="danger" text="report" /> <Badge type="warning" text="silent" /> Under C2-H-016, `sourceLines` on (0.1: `sourceLine`), with `\| a \| b \|`, a block image `![x](a.png)`, a line block or a footnote
Tool: Also on `<tbody>` and `<tr>`, and not on the bare `<img>`, the stanza `<p>` or the footnote `<li>`. Update readers of `data-source-line`.

::: compare no-render
```text
| a | b |
```
```text
<table>
  <tbody>
    <tr><td>a</td><td>b</td></tr>
  </tbody>
</table> With `sourceLines` on, C2-H-016 annotates `<tbody>` and `<tr>` as well as `<table>`, and annotates no bare block image, no `<p>` of a line block stanza and no `<li>` of the footnote section; the 0.1 option `sourceLine` annotated the table only and annotated those three. Readers of `data-source-line` have to expect the other elements.
```
:::

**U-288** <Badge type="danger" text="report" /> <Badge type="warning" text="silent" /> Under C2-H-016, an authored `data-source-line` with `sourceLines` on: `{data-source-line="99"}` above `p`
Tool: The generated value replaces it: `<p data-source-line="1">`. Without the option both write 99. Rename the authored key.

::: compare no-render
```text
{data-source-line="99"}
p
```
```text
<p data-source-line="99">p</p> With `sourceLines` on, the generated value replaces an authored `data-source-line` (C2-H-016), so the paragraph carries `data-source-line="1"`; the 0.1 option `sourceLine` kept the authored 99. Without the option both write the authored value. No 0.2 source keeps an authored value under the option.
```
:::

**U-293** <Badge type="danger" text="report" /> <Badge type="warning" text="silent" /> Under C2-H-165 and C2-H-163, a construct the profile does not admit, under `minimal` or `comment` (0.1: `Profile.minimal()`, `Profile.comment()`) and `article`
Tool: No placeholder word: a construct writes its plain text, behind the mark of its kind (`# `, `> `, `- `, `[img: ALT]`, so `[img: ]` for an empty alt), and an empty one writes nothing. Further degraded forms that differ, by input: A-18 `[](/u)` writes no text, and its paragraph renders nothing (C2-H-019); A-19 `{#note#}` gives no text, where 0.1 wrote `note`; A-22 `#tag` is text without `<span class="tag">`; A-23 a caption is one more paragraph, `<p>[img: x]</p>` and `<p>cap</p>`, where 0.1 wrote `[img: x] cap`; A-24 the lines of a line block are paragraphs, and a hard-break block joins its lines with spaces, where 0.1 wrote `<br>`; A-25 `:: x` and `: y` give `<p>x</p>` and `<p>y</p>`, where 0.1 wrote `x<br>` and `- y`; A-26 `\| a \| < \|` gives `a`, where 0.1 wrote `a \| `; A-30 a code block is one paragraph holding its line breaks, where 0.1 wrote `<br>`; A-31 under `article` an empty div and an empty quote are written, since the profile admits them, where 0.1 wrote nothing; A-32 under `article` a raw block is a paragraph of its value, where 0.1 wrote a code block with the format as its language. Review pages rendered under a profile.

:::: compare no-render
```text
:::
:::
```
```text
<div>

</div> Under `minimal` this empty div writes nothing: a node outside the profile writes its plain text and no placeholder word, and a node that holds no text writes nothing (C2-H-165). 0.1 wrote the node type in brackets for every degraded node without text: `[div]`, `[table]` for `||`, `[block_quote]` for `>`, `[code_block]` for an empty fence, `[link]` for `[](/u)`, `[text]` for each quote of `x.*/"q"/*`, and `[img]` for an image with no alt, where 0.2 writes `[img: ]`. The other degraded forms that differ are named in the UPGRADING.md row. No 0.2 source gives the placeholders.
```
::::

**U-341** <Badge type="danger" text="report" /> Under C2-H-126, the 0.1 placeholders `{user}` in `mentionUrl` and `{tag}` in `tagUrl`: `social: {mentionUrl: '/u/{user}'}` with `@alice`
Tool: `{name}` is the only placeholder; a template that holds any other is refused with `CarveOptionError`, so no link goes to a literal `{user}`. Write `{name}`.

::: compare no-render
```text
@alice and #news
```
```text
With `social: {mentionUrl: '/u/{user}'}` or `{tagUrl: '/t/{tag}'}` the render is refused with an option error: `{name}` is the only placeholder of a template (C2-H-126), and any other placeholder is refused rather than written into the `href`. 0.1 replaced `{user}` in `mentionUrl` and `{tag}` in `tagUrl` by the name, `<a class="mention" href="/u/alice">`. Write `{name}`.
```
:::
